title: Infinite families of affine primes force diagonal accumulation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $(\mathfrak p_n)_{n\geq1}$ be pairwise distinct prime ideals of $A$. For every $n$ fix a field embedding $k\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak p_n)$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak p_n)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_n)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. In the affine scheme $P=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product], let $E$ be the union, over $n\ne m$, of the images of $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(\mathfrak p_n)\otimes_k\kappa(\mathfrak p_m))\to P$ induced by the residue maps on the two factors. Then the Zariski closure $\overline E$ meets the image of the absolute diagonal $\operatorname{Spec}A\to P$, induced by multiplication $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to A$. No $k$-algebra structure on $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 088I (lemma-infinite-number); unadorned tensor products in the target are over Z, as in the proof of Tag 088J.

proof.text: Put $k_n=\kappa(\mathfrak p_n)$. Apply [lem-trf-family-common-extension-field] to the countable family $k_n/k$: obtain a field $K/k$ and compatible embeddings $i_n:k_n\hookrightarrow K$. Put $B=\prod_{n\geq1}K$ and define $\alpha:A\to B$ by $\alpha(a)_n=i_n(a\bmod\mathfrak p_n)$. This is a ring homomorphism; it does not require a $k$-algebra structure on $A$.

source.place: Tag 088I (lemma-infinite-number), product-of-fields proof; common-overfield refinement to use actual field-valued coordinate points.

proof.text:
Let $C=B\otimes_KB$, let $e_n$ be the coordinate idempotents, and put $J=(e_n\otimes e_n:n\geq1)$. By [lem-sfb-sequence-tensor-off-diagonal-kernel], the map $	heta:C	o\prod_{n
e m}K$, $u\otimes v\mapsto(u_nv_m)_{n
e m}$, has kernel $J$. Let $s_{n,m}\in\operatorname{Spec}C$ be the kernel of the coordinate map $	heta_{n,m}:C	o K$, and put $S=\{s_{n,m}:n
e m\}$. These kernels are prime because $K$ is a field.

source.place: Tag 088I (lemma-infinite-number), product-of-fields proof; common-overfield refinement to use actual field-valued coordinate points.

proof.text: The Zariski closure of $S$ is $V(J)$. Indeed, each $s_{n,m}$ contains $J$, so $\overline S\subseteq V(J)$. Conversely, if a closed set $V(H)$ contains $S$, every $h\in H$ has $\theta_{n,m}(h)=0$ for all $n\ne m$; hence $H\subseteq\ker\theta=J$, and $V(J)\subseteq V(H)$. Intersecting over all such closed sets gives the reverse containment. This uses only the definition of the Zariski topology; it makes no assertion about density for arbitrary products of nonreduced rings.

source.place: Tag 088I (lemma-infinite-number), product-of-fields proof; common-overfield refinement to use actual field-valued coordinate points.

proof.text: Let $I=(e_n:n\geq1)\subset B$. Every element of $I$ is a finite sum of multiples of $e_n$ and therefore has finite support. The constant sequence $1$ has infinite support, so $I\ne B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] choose a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ containing $I$. For the multiplication homomorphism $\mu:C\to B$, the prime $Q=\mu^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ contains $J$, since $\mu(e_n\otimes e_n)=e_n$. Thus $Q\in\overline S$.

source.place: Tag 088I (lemma-infinite-number), product-of-fields proof; common-overfield refinement to use actual field-valued coordinate points.

proof.text: Define $\psi:A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to C$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto\alpha(a)\otimes\alpha(b)$, and let $f=\operatorname{Spec}\psi$. For $n\ne m$, the homomorphism $k_n\otimes_k k_m\to K$, $x\otimes y\mapsto i_n(x)i_m(y)$, is well-defined by compatibility over $k$. Its composite with the residue map from $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A$ is $\theta_{n,m}\psi$, so $f(s_{n,m})\in E$. Continuity implies $f(Q)\in\overline E$: the closed set $f^{-1}(\overline E)$ contains $S$ and therefore its closure. Finally, $\mu\psi(a\otimes b)=\alpha(ab)$, so $f(Q)$ is the diagonal image of the prime $\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\in\operatorname{Spec}A$. This proves the required intersection.
